headline: Continued discussion of a proposed tenant rights ordinance until information is gathered from partners.
summary: Speakers discussed a proposed ordinance to protect tenant rights. Topics included notice to tenants, enforcement, tying the rules to occupancy permits, and dispute resolution. The group voted to hold further discussion after gathering information from different partners.
decisions: Continued discussion of the proposed tenant rights ordinance until information is gathered from different partners, approved by voice vote.

transcript:
# Lowell City Council
## Housing SC Meeting Minutes

**Date:** October 13, 2026
**Time:** 5:30 PM
**Location:** Council Chamber, City Hall / Zoom (Hybrid)

## PRESENT:

Present on Roll Call were C. Robinson, C. Chau and C. Nuon. Also, present Yovani Baez-Rose (DPD), City Solicitor Williams, Asst. City Solicitor French, C. McDonough, C. Liang and Edward Mierzwa (Building Inspector).

## MEETING CALLED TO ORDER:

C. Robinson called the meeting to order noting attendance and the ordinance regarding tenant rights referred to the subcommittee.

## ORDER OF BUSINESS:

C. Robinson opened matter to the public; Aaron Ginsburg (Community Teamwork, Inc.) commented on the proposed ordinance noting his input and indicating the goal is ensuring tenants are educated concerning their rights. C. Robinson outlined the drafting of the ordinance. City Solicitor Williams commented on the drafting of the ordinance and that it originated from third party source, but fundamentally good and purpose was clear. C. Robinson questioned application of the ordinance by private and public entities, noting some exemptions in the language. Asst. Solicitor French noted the application to all entities. C. Robinson commented on the fines / warnings in place and questioned the enforcement procedures for this ordinance. Mr. Ginsberg suggested tying it to occupancy permits. Mr. Mierzwa outlined the permitting process in the City which focus on safety and health and that permits stay with the unit until they expire. C. Robinson noted the need for a notice element for the ordinance. C. Chau recognized the importance of tenant rights and the need for enforcement of them. C. Chau noted the need to explore ways to inform tenants of these rights and must be applicable to all landlords. Ms. Baez-Rose indicated many forums in which to provide notice to tenants. Ms. Baez-Rose noted the need for oversight if there is to be full compliance. City Solicitor Williams indicated further discussion regarding tracking information. Asst. City Solicitor French commented on some options discussed. C. Nuon recognized the motion was made by C. McDonough and that it is a good ordinance to protect tenant rights. C. Nuon noted larger complexes are usually compliant with the state rules and regulations as they have the resources and that smaller landlords may have difficulty. C. Noun suggested language regarding short term rentals should be excluded from ordinance as they are not allowed in the City. C. Chau noted the need for some type of dispute resolution.

C. Robinson opened back up to public: Jeff Bush (Heritage Properties) noted he was a large landlord in the City and that the industry was highly regulated regarding tenant rights. Mr. Bush noted that landlords can add to this discussion. Mikeala Hondros-McCarthy noted she was a small landlord noted it is in the best interest to have informed tenants and safe properties. C. Robinson noted the community needs to be involved with this discussion as it develops. Ms. Baez-Rose noted the ability to inform partners. **Motion** by C. Nuon, seconded by C. Chau to have further subcommittee discussion once information is gathered from different partners. So voted.

## ADJOURNMENT:

**Motion** to adjourn by C. Chau, seconded by C. Nuon. So Voted.

Meeting adjourned at 6:29 PM

Michael Q. Geary, City Clerk
